common_name: Blue Lady Browallia (Violet-Blue Amethyst Flower with Cream Eye)

planting.note: Press seed onto the surface of moist starting mix without covering, since light aids germination; transplant seedlings out once frost danger has fully passed.

directions: Blue Lady is a heirloom-type selection of the taller, willowy Browallia americana rather than the compact bedding hybrids, producing violet-blue flowers set off by a pale creamy throat along branching stems. It tolerates more sun than most bush violets and holds up well to heat, though flower color and plant vigor stay best where afternoon shade is available in hot regions. Pinch young plants after transplanting to build a fuller, bushier framework before bloom sets in, and it will often self-sow a new generation true to type where winters allow. Once established it shrugs off short dry spells better than the fussier speciosa hybrids, though steady moisture keeps bloom densest.

common_name: Endless Celebration Browallia (Light Lavender Reblooming Bush Violet)

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after the last frost into humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this University of New Hampshire-bred selection, sold under the trade name Endless Celebration, holds a tidy, rounded shape without staking.

directions: Endless Celebration carries numerous single flowers in a soft light lavender with a darker rim around each petal, a subtler tone than the deeper blue-purple of its sibling Endless Illumination. Bred for stems that resist splitting apart at the crown as the plant matures, it keeps a neat, rounded outline in hanging baskets and mixed containers without staking or hard pinching. Give it partial shade and consistently moist, well-drained soil, since it flowers continuously through the season without deadheading but declines quickly if allowed to dry out repeatedly. Light monthly feeding sustains the bloom show from spring planting through the first fall frost.
